declared_purpose: Manage and back up QQ Zone albums through QR login, album/photo browsing, uploads, downloads and album creation. Cookie-based authorization and automatic local cookie saving are explicit requirements; public visibility and enriched responses are implementation choices (SKILL.md:3-9,47-63). The documentation claims credentials remain local, but the implementation supplies authentication to QQ services (SKILL.md:116-119; README.md:110-113; scripts/qzone_photos.py:89-96,597-624).

data_operations.operation: Read local credentials and prepare an authenticated session
data_operations.source: The --cookies JSON file, defaulting to cookies.json
data_operations.data_scope: Entire JSON file is loaded; p_skey, skey and uin populate cookies, with uin also copied to p_uin. Cookies are configured for .qq.com.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory and requests.Session cookie jar; subsequent network operations are described separately.
data_operations.condition: Every non-login CLI action, before action-specific argument validation; execution requires p_skey.

data_operations.operation: Derive authentication tokens and normalize an account identifier
data_operations.source: p_skey, qrsig, uin and optional qq_number or --qq
data_operations.data_scope: g_tk and ptqrtoken are credential-derived tokens. QQ number is selected explicitly or normalized from uin; this is identifier processing, not demographic inference.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory; tokens and identifiers are used in the applicable QQ requests. Login also saves the normalized QQ number.
data_operations.condition: g_tk and account selection occur for non-login actions; ptqrtoken occurs during QR polling; account normalization also occurs after successful login.

data_operations.operation: Fetch a login QR code, poll authentication and follow a response-selected URL
data_operations.source: QQ login responses and the login session cookie jar
data_operations.data_scope: QR image, qrsig, derived ptqrtoken, login status, redirect URL and applicable session cookies.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ssl.ptlogin2.qq.com/ptqrshow and /ptqrlogin; after success, the HTTP(S) host extracted from the response. Response data and cookies enter local memory.
data_operations.condition: login action; polling makes up to 120 attempts. The success URL has no host allowlist; its GET explicitly disables automatic redirects.

data_operations.operation: Persist and display the login QR image
data_operations.data_scope: Complete QR image, its filesystem path and a terminal rendering of its modules.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/qq_login_qr.png, the local default image viewer and CLI stdout; Pillow reads the saved image locally.
data_operations.condition: QR fetch returns HTTP 200. Viewer opening and terminal rendering are both attempted. The supplied login return paths contain no QR-file deletion.

data_operations.source: Cookies collected from the login session and success response
data_operations.data_scope: qq_number, p_skey, skey and uin; only these selected fields are saved.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The --cookies JSON path, written as plaintext and replacing existing file contents. The dictionary also returns to the local caller.
data_operations.condition: Login reports success and supplies a matching redirect URL. Automatic cookie saving is explicitly documented; no expiration-based deletion is implemented here.

data_operations.data_scope: qq_number, p_skey, skey and uin, serialized without redaction.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout and its invoking caller. Further logging or external forwarding is not shown.
data_operations.condition: Successful CLI login, after the credential file has been saved.

data_operations.source: Selected QQ account, authenticated session and QQ album response
data_operations.data_scope: Request includes account identifiers, g_tk and needUserInfo=1. Local processing selects album IDs, names, counts, creation/modification times and descriptions.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated GET to https://h5.qzone.qq.com/proxy/domain/photo.qzone.qq.com/fcgi-bin/fcg_list_album_v3; response enters local memory and selected results reach caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: list action. Whether additional user information is actually returned is not established.

data_operations.source: Selected account and album ID, authenticated session and QQ photo response
data_operations.data_scope: Request includes account identifiers, album ID, g_tk, a default page size of 500 and need_private_comment=1. Selected results contain photo identifiers, names, descriptions, preferred image URLs, dimensions and upload times; comments are not selected.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated GET to https://h5.qzone.qq.com/proxy/domain/photo.qzone.qq.com/fcgi-bin/cgi_list_photo; response enters local memory. photos prints selected results; download-album consumes them locally.
data_operations.condition: photos or download-album action. Actual private-comment response contents are unknown.

data_operations.operation: Request remote album creation with public visibility
data_operations.source: --title, optional --desc, selected QQ account and authenticated session
data_operations.data_scope: Album title, description, account identifiers, g_tk and priv=1, which the source labels public.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated POST to https://h5.qzone.qq.com/proxy/domain/photo.qzone.qq.com/fcgi-bin/fcg_create_album. This requests remote storage and public visibility; actual access and retention depend on QQ. Parsed response reaches caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: create action with a title; no CLI privacy option is provided.

data_operations.operation: Read and upload the selected photo
data_operations.source: --photo file, optional album ID and authenticated session
data_operations.data_scope: Original file bytes and basename, QQ identifiers, optional album ID, g_tk, p_skey and skey. There is no metadata-stripping step. A QQ-based backUrls value is a form field, not evidence of another HTTP request.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Multipart POST to https://up.qzone.qq.com/cgi-bin/upload/cgi_upload_image, requesting remote photo storage. Credentials appear in form fields as well as the configured session cookie jar. Upload results return to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: upload action with an existing file. If album ID is omitted, destination-album selection is left to the service.

data_operations.source: --url or a URL selected from the photo-list response
data_operations.data_scope: Requested URL, fixed browser/Qzone headers, applicable session cookies and downloaded bytes. MIME type or local magic bytes may infer an extension; this only renames the file.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GET to the supplied URL's host using the shared session. Cookies are configured for .qq.com, not every arbitrary host. Bytes are written under the constructed output path; paths and download errors are printed locally.
data_operations.condition: download, or each usable photo URL during download-album. HTTP 200 is required before writing. Files are opened with replacement semantics; no post-download deletion is implemented.

data_operations.source: One list_photos result and its server-provided photo names
data_operations.data_scope: Returned photo URLs, names and downloaded content; output includes names, local file paths and counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Files beneath os.path.join(output_dir, album_id), with each photo name passed directly into destination-path construction; results reach caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: download-album. Only one listing call is made, using the default requested page size of 500; complete backup of larger albums is unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Return server diagnostics to the invoking caller
data_operations.source: Album, photo, creation and upload HTTP responses
data_operations.data_scope: Up to 500 characters of unparsed response text; creation and some upload paths also return complete parsed objects. Actual diagnostic contents are unavailable.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local function caller and, through CLI result serialization, stdout. No separate diagnostic collector is shown.
data_operations.condition: Parsing failures or the applicable creation/upload response branches.

potential_excess.data_scope: p_skey, skey and uin in the successful login JSON
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout / invoking caller, beyond the required cookie-file persistence
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Login must authenticate and automatically save cookies; the entry does not require printing credential values.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Save usable credentials and report success. The function's ordinary return to its caller is a separate boundary.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Print a success status and cookie-file path instead of serializing credentials; retain the internal return if needed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the saved credential format and subsequent authenticated actions working. Do not assume stdout is externally forwarded.

potential_excess.data_scope: Login QR image after its scanning purpose ends
potential_excess.condition: Any successful QR-image fetch, including later login failure, expiration or timeout
potential_excess.purpose_basis: QR login needs temporary scan presentation; indefinite image retention is not required.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the image available while scanning is possible.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a temporary file with cleanup on all completion and failure paths.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not remove the image before the selected viewer or terminal presentation can make it scannable.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second presentation of the same login QR image
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Both the local default image viewer and terminal stdout
potential_excess.condition: _display_qr attempts viewer opening and then terminal rendering
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Scanning requires a usable presentation, not necessarily both presentations. This is a potentially redundant action, rather than extra fields in a required request.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide one usable QR presentation with an appropriate fallback.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Select a display channel and use the other as an explicit or failure fallback.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Support both graphical and headless environments; successful process launch alone does not prove the viewer was usable.

potential_excess.data_scope: Additional user information requested through needUserInfo=1
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Potential additional fields returned by the album-list endpoint into local process memory; they are not selected for album output
potential_excess.condition: list action, if the QQ endpoint honors the flag
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Album listing consumes album metadata, not separate user-profile information.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the album-list request and required album fields.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Disable or omit user-information enrichment if supported. This narrows response data rather than removing the required request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: API behavior must be validated; the supplied source does not prove what the flag returns or whether it is optional.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Potential comment fields returned by cgi_list_photo into local process memory; selected photo results omit comments
potential_excess.condition: photos and download-album, if the endpoint honors the flag
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Browsing and downloading photos use photo metadata and image URLs; private comments are not consumed.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain photo listing and the metadata/URLs needed for the chosen action.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Disable or omit private-comment enrichment if the API supports it. Keep the necessary listing request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm the reduced request preserves accessible photos and required metadata; actual comment delivery and flag semantics are unresolved.

potential_excess.data_scope: Created album metadata and its requested visibility
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: QQ album service with priv=1, labeled public by the source; actual public access remains unverified
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Creating an album does not itself require public sharing; visibility is hardcoded rather than selected by the user.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Create the requested album with its title and description.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Expose a visibility choice and use a restricted default when no sharing requirement exists.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Honor explicit sharing requests and confirm the chosen setting permits intended uploads and owner access. Do not assume actual server permissions from the comment alone.

potential_excess.data_scope: p_skey, skey, uin and p_uin made available to photo-download requests
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The --url host or returned photo-URL host when it matches the configured .qq.com cookie scope; this is broader than a fixed set of authenticated Qzone endpoints
potential_excess.condition: download or download-album targets a matching host using the shared session
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Fetching the selected photo does not establish that every matching QQ host needs all account cookies.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Perform the selected image GET and provide authentication where that image actually requires it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use an unauthenticated download session for public images and explicitly scoped, minimal authentication for verified protected image hosts.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve protected downloads and required service headers. Actual hosts and authentication requirements are unknown; cookies are not shown being sent to arbitrary non-QQ hosts.

potential_excess.data_scope: Downloaded photo bytes written outside the intended backup directory
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The path produced by joining output_dir, album_id and the unvalidated server-provided photo name
potential_excess.condition: An album ID or returned photo name contains an absolute path or parent-directory components accepted by the host filesystem
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Album backup requires persistence within the chosen output boundary; path construction does not enforce that boundary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Save all selected photos in the caller-selected backup location.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate album directory components, sanitize photo filenames and enforce destination containment beneath the selected output root.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve explicit --output choices and handle filename collisions without losing photos.

unknowns: QQ endpoint implementations are absent. Their requirements block confirming whether user-information/private-comment flags or duplicated upload authentication fields can be removed while preserving functionality.
Actual login-success and photo URL hosts are response-dependent. Dependency-level cookie, redirect and network behavior beyond the visible configuration is not supplied.
Actual public access, remote retention, deletion and downstream processing by QQ cannot be established. The upload destination album and visibility when album_id is omitted are also unspecified.
No real photo or response payloads are supplied. Embedded photo metadata, actual enriched profile/comment fields and sensitive content in raw diagnostic snippets are therefore unknown.
Default viewer behavior, third-party dependency internals and downstream caller logging are outside the supplied source. Local display and stdout do not establish additional remote disclosure.
Full-album backup completeness remains unresolved: list_photos requests 500 entries by default and download_album makes one listing call without pagination (scripts/qzone_photos.py:422-436,546-579).
